summary: Since ansible-core 2.11, playbooks in a collection can be referenced by FQCN from the CLI or import_playbook, keeping collection context. They must live in playbooks/ and should take hosts from a variable to avoid hitting all inventory.
questions: How do I run a playbook that ships inside a collection?
Can I import_playbook from a collection by name?
How should collection playbooks define their target hosts?
Can collection playbooks have a roles subdirectory?

answer_card.title: Playbooks in collections
answer_card.answer_md:
- Since **ansible-core 2.11**, use `namespace.collection.playbook` (extension optional) on the command line or with `import_playbook`; it runs in collection context.
- Keep them in `playbooks/`; `files/`, `vars/`, `templates/` are fine but not `roles/`.
- Make hosts a variable, e.g. `hosts: '{{target|default("all")}}'`, so users don't hit all inventory by accident. Users can then pass `-e` or `--limit`.
- Document usage in `docs/` or the README.
